newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Stevens sets bankruptcy plan to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Stevens sets bankruptcy plan to cut debt.

text.p: The parent of J.P. Stevens, one of the nation's largest textiles manufacturers, plans to file a prepackaged bankruptcy plan to help eliminate debt incurred in its 1988 buyout, the company said Friday.

JPS Textile Group reached an agreement with its debt holders that would restructure the company, Chief Executive Jerry Hunter said, giving debt holders most of the new common stock of the restructured company.
Under the restructuring, JPS Textile said, its operating subsidiaries will have a new revolving credit facility. JPS Textile, based in Greenville, S.C., has annual revenues of about $450 million.
Holders of JPS Textile's bonds will get $10 million to $14 million in cash, new notes and about 93 percent of the company's new common stock.
The company said other noteholders will get almost 6 percent of the new stock and senior management will receive 0.75 percent.

As a result, the agreement would create a new capital structure while the company's operating units continued business as usual, alleviating uncertainties associated with upcoming debt maturities, Hunter said.

JPS Textile will then have the financial resources to make capital investments in its operating businesses to better position the company for long-term profitability and growth, he said in a statement.
JPS said it has an agreement in principle with an unofficial committee of bondholders, representing more than 60 percent of its outstanding public debt.

In the meantime, the JPS Textile's existing debt facility has been extended through July 16 to enable the company to complete the prepackaged Chapter 11 filing. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.
If JPS Textile starts a Chapter 11 case by July 16, the revolving credit facility will be extended automatically, the company said.
The agreement also calls for the election of a new board.

Currently, JPS Textile has outstanding bond debt of $76.8 million on its senior subordinated notes; $109.2 million on its senior subordinated discount notes; and $54.1 million on its subordinated debentures.
Spokeswoman Wendi Kopsick said 34 percent of the common is held by Odyssey Partners and 17 percent by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
